stem: A vehicle travels at 60 mph on a level road. Using a perception-reaction time of 2.5 s and a deceleration rate of 11.2 ft/s^{2}, what is the stopping sight distance?
eli5: Stopping sight distance has two parts: the distance covered at full speed during perception and reaction, 1.47 V t, and the braking distance, V^{2} / (30 (a/32.2 ± G)). With V in mph the constants give feet. On a level road the grade term G is zero.

stem: What is the minimum radius of a horizontal curve for a design speed of 50 mph, with a superelevation of 6% and a side friction factor of 0.14?
eli5: On a horizontal curve the centripetal force is supplied by superelevation and side friction together. Balancing them gives the minimum radius R = V^{2} / (15 (e + f)), with V in mph, R in feet and e as a decimal.

stem: An intersection approach carries 1,200 vehicles in the peak hour. The busiest 15 minutes of that hour carries 375 vehicles. What is the peak hour factor?
eli5: The peak hour factor compares the hourly volume with the flow rate of the busiest 15 minutes: PHF = V / (4 × V_{15}). A value of 1.0 means perfectly even flow; lower values mean sharper peaking. Dividing a volume by the PHF gives the design flow rate.

stem: A crest vertical curve connects a +3% grade to a -2% grade and is 500 ft long. How far from the start of the curve (PVC) is the high point?
eli5: A vertical curve is a parabola, so its grade changes at a constant rate r = (g_{2} - g_{1}) / L. The high or low point is where the grade reaches zero: x = -g_{1} / r = g_{1} L / (g_{1} - g_{2}).

stem: Which of these are regulatory signs under the MUTCD? Select the three that apply.

options.text: Curve sign on a yellow diamond

eli5: Regulatory signs give orders you can be ticketed for ignoring. Warning signs give a heads-up. Guide signs help you find your way.
solution:
STOP, YIELD and Speed Limit signs state traffic laws, so they are regulatory.

A curve sign on a yellow diamond is a warning sign. A street name sign is a guide sign.

verify.basis: MUTCD Part 2: Chapter 2B regulatory signs (STOP R1-1, YIELD R1-2, Speed Limit R2-1), Chapter 2C warning signs, Chapter 2D guide signs

stem: Which of these are warning signs under the MUTCD? Select the three that apply.
eli5: The MUTCD sorts signs by function. Warning signs alert drivers to conditions ahead and are mostly yellow diamonds with black legends; pedestrian and school warnings may be fluorescent yellow-green. Regulatory signs state laws and are mostly white rectangles. Guide signs give directions.
solution:
The Curve sign, the Signal Ahead sign and the Pedestrian Crossing sign are all warning signs.

Speed Limit and Do Not Enter are regulatory signs.

verify.basis: MUTCD Part 2, Chapter 2C warning signs (Curve W1-2, Signal Ahead W3-3, Pedestrian Crossing W11-2); Chapter 2B regulatory signs (Speed Limit R2-1, Do Not Enter R5-1)

stem: A flexible pavement has 4 in of asphalt (layer coefficient 0.44), 8 in of base (0.14) and 10 in of subbase (0.11). Drainage coefficients are 1.0. What is the structural number?
eli5: In the AASHTO flexible pavement method, each layer contributes its thickness times a layer coefficient that reflects its relative strength, and unbound layers are also multiplied by a drainage coefficient. The sum is the structural number, SN.

stem: A signalized approach has 2 lanes, each with a saturation flow rate of 1,900 veh/h. The approach gets 40 s of effective green in a 100 s cycle. What is its capacity?
eli5: A signalized lane group can only discharge during its effective green. Capacity is the saturation flow rate times the share of the cycle that is green: c = N s (g / C).

stem: A road follows the Greenshields model with a free-flow speed of 60 mph and a jam density of 120 veh/mi. What is its capacity?
eli5: Greenshields assumes speed falls linearly with density. Flow = density × speed is then a parabola that peaks at half the jam density and half the free-flow speed, so capacity = u_{f} k_{j} / 4.
solution:
At capacity: k = 120 / 2 = 60 veh/mi and u = 60 / 2 = 30 mph.

q_{max} = 60 × 30 = \frac{60(120)}{4} = 1,800 veh/h.

stem: A signal approach has a speed of 30 mph (44 ft/s) on level ground. Using a perception-reaction time of 1.0 s and a deceleration rate of 10 ft/s^{2}, what yellow change interval is needed?
eli5: The yellow interval must cover the driver's reaction time plus the time to decelerate to a stop, so that a driver too close to stop can enter legally: y = t + v / (2a + 2 g G), with v in ft/s. On level ground the grade term is zero.

stem: An intersection has 12 crashes in one year. Its entering volume is 20,000 vehicles per day. What is the crash rate per million entering vehicles?
eli5: Crash rates normalise crash counts by exposure so that sites with different volumes can be compared. For intersections: rate = crashes × 1,000,000 / (ADT × 365 × years).
solution:
Entering vehicles in one year = 20,000 × 365 = 7,300,000.

Rate = \frac{12 × 1,000,000}{7,300,000} = 1.64 crashes per million entering vehicles.

stem: A logit mode choice model gives a utility of -0.5 for auto and -1.5 for bus. What share of travellers choose the bus?
eli5: The multinomial logit model gives each mode a share proportional to e raised to its utility: P(mode) = e^{U} / (sum of e^{U} over all modes). Only differences in utility matter.

stem: A horizontal curve has a radius of 1,000 ft and a deflection angle of 30°. What is the length of the curve?
eli5: The length of a circular curve is the arc subtended by the deflection (central) angle: L = R × angle in radians = R × Δ × π / 180.

stem: A horizontal curve has a radius of 1,000 ft and a deflection angle of 30°. What is the tangent length from the PC to the PI?
eli5: The two tangents meet at the PI. Each tangent, from PC to PI or PI to PT, has length T = R tan(Δ / 2), from the right triangle formed by the radius, the tangent and the line from the centre to the PI.

stem: A crest vertical curve joins grades of +2% and -3%. The design requires a rate of vertical curvature K of 150. What minimum curve length is needed?
eli5: K is the horizontal length of curve needed for each 1% of grade change, chosen from the design speed to provide sight distance. Curve length = K × A, where A is the algebraic difference in grades in percent.
